claims.value: The new explicit operator constraint replaces the open-ended alpha soak with a 30-minute dev-only trial: no production changes or durable controller persistence; start with batch ceiling 128 and adaptive fetch; accept only with at least 900 PGCR/sec steady during the final 10 minutes, zero integrity/recovery violations, no DB connection failure storm, and successful restart from DB truth after the controlled stop.

The bounded-alpha constraint changes experiment scope, not historical evidence or authority: DB rows remain truth, raw marker commits travel with summaries, failures retry, availability failure stops rather than spins, and restart scans gaps. It grants no authority for production changes, durable persistence, rebuild/recompute paths, parser-state correctness tables, or Cortex S3 replay into DB writes.

answer.answer: Revised child checkpoint committed as checkpoint:5ea08bc6-79fe-2876-cfd5-27e1e2319d47. The buildable layout uses three level-0 cores, with one heavy machine per core.

claims.value: The recovered architecture is an Update 1-only modular backbone-and-spurs factory: rails distribute items and power, Rail v.1 is the starting tier, v.2/v.3 are used only when measured flow requires 240/480 items per minute, and production remains distributed rather than consolidated into a mega-base.

Revision N+1 requires one Constructorizer and two Facturers while every Base Core stays level 0. Their heavy-machine heat is 500 + 650 + 650 = 1,800, versus 1,000 capacity per level-0 core. Constructorizer plus Facturer is 1,150, two Facturers are 1,300, and all three are 1,800; each combination exceeds one core and would disable Fire Wave protection.

The safe revised layout uses three occupied level-0 cores: Core A contains only the Constructorizer at 500/1,000 heavy-machine heat, Core B contains Facturer 1 at 650/1,000, and Core C contains Facturer 2 at 650/1,000. Before ancillary loads, their remaining capacity is 500, 350, and 350 respectively; all unsafe heavy-machine co-location is rejected.

Before construction, inventory the existing and planned heat-bearing load at each candidate core and verify every total remains at or below 1,000 with Fire Wave protection active. Then commission one cell at a time and recheck its load after every placement. The revision delta controls requirements, saved Update 1 evidence controls heat/capacity and rail facts, and hidden, future, pre-Update-1, or unverified amplifier equipment cannot be used to make the plan pass.

checkpoint.objective: Operate one Constructorizer and two Facturers in a distributed Update 1 factory while every Base Core remains level 0 and every occupied core retains Fire Wave protection.
current_state: The parent backbone-and-spurs architecture remains valid.

decisions: Use three occupied level-0 cores: Constructorizer at Core A, Facturer 1 at Core B, and Facturer 2 at Core C.
Reject Constructorizer-plus-Facturer, Facturer-plus-Facturer, and three-machine co-location because each exceeds 1,000 heat.
Count all ancillary heat against the host core and do not rely on hidden, future, pre-Update-1, or unverified capacity equipment.

Place and commission one heavy machine per core, confirming Fire Wave protection after every placement.
Connect cells with Update 1 rails and upgrade trunks only when measured throughput requires v.2 or v.3.

answer.answer: Advanced Straylight from evaluation into implementation and committed child checkpoint checkpoint:6370212d-80b3-98a6-70a3-bc04ef6ff23c at corpus generation 717882.

claims.value: Straylight is an agent-first portable context and durable-work layer—not primarily a notes, retrieval, or memory-database product. It preserves learned knowledge and live resumable work state, including evidence, decisions, artifacts, computations, checkpoints, unresolved questions, and safe next actions, with provenance and full sources retained.

Cumulative cached replay and uncached per-case input are different token measures and must be reported separately; cached replay cannot substantiate an uncached-input advantage. The frozen one-shot BM25 regression baseline passed 17/20 cases, recovered 48/53 evidence items, and used about 1,070 mean estimated tokens, versus 17/20, 46/53, and about 2,932 for the tuned stateful prototype. BM25 remains a regression fixture, not the target architecture.

The first persistent build slice is a typed, service-backed vertical path that reopens a parent checkpoint in a snapshot-pinned workspace, explicitly refreshes N to N+1 and returns the diff, batches query/read operations, combines exact and lexical retrieval behind a pluggable semantic path, and commits an immutable child naming its parent and preserving exact source references. Semantic failure must degrade explicitly while exact and lexical retrieval remain usable; storage engine and semantic-provider selection remain deferred.

The transition gate passes only when every case matches the direct-filesystem answer claims in no more than four completed workspace calls; proves parent-at-N reopening, explicit N+1 refresh and diff, exact-plus-lexical retrieval with a pluggable semantic path, batched query/read, immutable parent-and-source lineage, and no full-corpus reconstruction when checkpoint plus delta suffice; and reports cumulative cached replay separately from uncached input alongside the BM25 baseline.

Judge acceptance by direct-filesystem claim parity and transition behavior, not retrieval score or token count alone.
